description: Multi-interface Sub-lemma 2.1: operator-valued A^λ_{ξν}(I_2) extraction at H_9 ↓ H_6 × H_3 for I_2 = pn. Phase 1 (tractable scope) with K_6 = 12, K_3 = 12 test words. Low-dim λ ⊢ 9 are over-determined and reach machine-ε consistency; high-dim λ (e.g. (4,3,1,1) with d_λ=216) are under-determined at this K and flagged. Phase 2 (K = 60+) deferred.

deprecated.reason: np.linalg.lstsq on dense complex systems, residual ~1e-14. A genuine float64 COMPUTATION, not a float64 exit -- there is no higher-precision value being cast away here. An mpmath rewrite is not available at any budget: mp.qr_solve at 50 dps measures 2.62 / 8.91 / 21.32 / 76.65 s at n_unknowns 64 / 96 / 128 / 192, a fitted exponent of 3.07, and the largest real block is 3,390 unknowns -- ~145 h for one block, ~17,000 h across 30 blocks x 4 witnesses. Robust to the exponent: even at n^2 it is ~500 h. Bean qou-1lr8.
deprecated.not_production: Reachability established by reading the CONTROL FLOW, not by grep and not by import cone -- both of those gave wrong answers first, in opposite directions (qou-1lr8 records them). canonical_tr_m_via_branching sets n = 3*A and returns via the fine-Bratteli transfer for A >= 3 BEFORE the extract load, so the load is reached only at A == 2 where n is always 6. NO H_9 entry is reachable from it, and the canonical mass table reaches these witnesses only through that function. The two real consumers -- sublemma_2_1_h9_tritium_verify.py and sublemma_2_1_h12_helium_4_framework.py -- are ANCHOR-ONLY: neither contains q_val, q0, Q_MP or Q_50_DIGIT anywhere, so the hybrid-off-anchor failure mode qou-8chw fixed for the deuteron cannot arise. Closes that bean's surviving item.

caveats: Phase 1 scope: K_6 = K_3 = 12 test words gives 144 equations per λ. The high-dim ξ = (3,2,1) (d=16) supports up to 16²·2² = 1024 unknowns per block, exceeding 144 — those λ are under-determined and their A_per_pair summaries reflect a least-squares projection, not a unique extraction. Phase 2 (K ≥ 60) is needed for the high-dim λ subset.

At q_0 the bilinear system uses numpy complex (f64). Verification of the iterated Sub-lemma 2.1 formula at machine ε is bounded by f64 precision (~1e-12 relative). An mpmath 50-dps version of this extraction would push the floor to ~1e-45 but at substantially higher cost; deferred to follow-up if 1-ppb mass-prediction work requires it.
